name: District of Columbia

regulator.name: DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection (DLCP)

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act, amended toward RUAAA (D.C. Code 47-2887 and following)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. D.C. Code 47-2889.02 says NIL agents must register.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student-athlete in your sport.
summary: Register online with DLCP. $400. Expires May 31 of even years.

steps.text: Fill out the Initial Athlete Agent Application online
steps.detail: Have a 2x2 photo, a government ID and a resume of your training, education and experience.
Includes the $100 application fee. Not refundable.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This counts for contact through a parent or anyone else too. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, any other pay you get, that you're registered in D.C. and where else, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the bold Warning to Student-Athlete notice in the contract
steps.detail: Use the exact words D.C. gives. If the athlete is a minor, reword it for the parent.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. If the athlete is a minor, a parent or guardian signs it and the contract.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
steps.detail: Give it to the parent or guardian if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Notify the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete (or a parent, for a minor) may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: If the athlete enrolls at a new school, tell its athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The clock starts when you learn they enrolled. If you knew them before they got a sports scholarship, tell that school within 10 days.

steps.text: Help the athlete report NIL deals to the school before they get paid
steps.detail: The athlete must share each deal over $300, your name and a copy of your agent agreement. Changes are due within 10 days.

steps.text: Sign the statement in each NIL deal that it is the sole, complete and final agreement
steps.detail: Every NIL deal needs this statement. The athlete, the company and you (if you worked on the deal) all make it.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs. The city can inspect them.

steps.text: Never lie or make false promises to sign an athlete
steps.detail: Don't give anything that could cost eligibility unless you tell the athletic director within 72 hours and the athlete signs a written OK.

steps.text: Charge an NIL fee that is normal for your industry
steps.detail: D.C. requires it but sets no number.

steps.text: Don't set up NIL deals for alcohol, tobacco, vaping, drugs, betting, guns or adult entertainment
steps.detail: D.C. bans these deals for college athletes. Deals also can't pay the athlete to pick or stay at a school.
Every even year. The next renewal is May 31, 2028.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: DLCP lists a $400 registration fee and a $100 application fee "to be included with" it. Call DLCP at 202-671-4500 to confirm the total is $400, not $500.
